content: Deep learning systems have shown a lot of promise for extractive Question Answering (QA), with performance comparable to humans when large scale data is available. However, practitioners looking to build QA systems for specific applications may not have the resources to collect tens of thousands of questions on corpora of their choice. At the same time, state-of-the-art machine reading systems do not lend well to low-resource QA settings where the number of labeled question-answer pairs are limited (c.f. Table 2 ). Semi-supervised QA methods like BIBREF0 aim to improve this performance by leveraging unlabeled data which is easier to collect.
